title: Validating the Comparison, Not Just the Scorer: Why Overall Accuracy Can Mislead in Interactive LLM Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.31678v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many LLM studies compare how models respond to different follow-up prompts. For example, one prompt may neutrally ask a model to reconsider, while another insists that an invented film really exists. The difference is used to measure the effect of conversational pressure. abstract: arXiv:2610.31679v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as math tutors, raising two questions: can a single LLM detect a student's error, diagnose the underlying misconception, and remediate it through multi-turn dialogue - and can we trust the numbers that report how well it does? title: Rethinking Structured Generation: Can Graph-Based Reasoning Resolve Ambiguity?
abstract: arXiv:2610.31681v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Structured generation is typically formulated as a deterministic mapping from input to a single structured output. title: Multi modal perceived conversation success prediction for spontaneous autistic and non-autistic dyadic interactions
abstract: arXiv:2610.31682v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Conversation success is important for communication, social bonds, and well-being and is often reduced in autistic-neurotypical conversations. Previous studies have predicted perceived conversation success using acoustic and lexical features in pediatric autism-enriched samples, or using nonverbal behavior in non-autistic group interactions. abstract: arXiv:2610.31683v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Persona-conditioned language models are used as simulated patients and affective agents, but there is no validated way to ask whether a belief assigned to such a model organizes its behaviour or whether the model has merely adopted a mood. title: Knowledge Graphs Quality Assessment in the Era of LLMs: A Conceptual Framework
abstract: arXiv:2610.31684v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) have been popularized during the last few decades and are increasingly constructed and consumed by Large Language Models (LLMs). abstract: arXiv:2610.31685v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based multimodal emotion reasoning systems perform well on standard benchmarks, but improving them through instruction tuning can be computationally expensive. title: From Target Selection to Condition Reuse: Auditing Residual Interventions in Tool-Use Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.31686v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Activation interventions can make a language model produce a target answer, but can the model use the intended condition in other computations? title: Distributional Alignment of LLMs and Its Generalization Properties
abstract: arXiv:2610.31687v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate and probe human behavior, e.g., for surveys. For these applications, a key property is that outputs satisfy distributional alignment: to match its output distribution with some reference (in this case, human) distribution. abstract: arXiv:2610.31701v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Enterprise customer journeys are shaped not only by product experiences and marketing, but also by recurring resource-allocation decisions. In B2B go-to-market (GTM) organizations, territory carving determines which accounts receive seller coverage, which seller-account relationships are preserved, and how limited field capacity is distributed. title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2610.31702v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. However, most existing methods follow a supervised learning paradigm that requires costly labeled data and task-specific model training. abstract: arXiv:2610.31704v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage. abstract: arXiv:2610.31716v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. abstract: arXiv:2610.31718v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Financial transaction networks are naturally represented as multigraphs, where repeated transactions between the same pair of accounts are modeled as distinct edges. abstract: arXiv:2610.31721v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Optimizing high-dimensional physical systems under expensive evaluations and complex constraints is a central challenge in science and engineering. title: Autoregressive Multimodal Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models for Microservice Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.31722v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Microservice systems have become a dominant architecture for large-scale cloud applications, enabling rapid deployment and elastic scaling. abstract: arXiv:2610.31723v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This article introduces Latin Modern BERT (LAMB), an encoder for the Latin language based on the ModernBERT architecture, pretrained in two phases on more than 74B Latin tokens using a novel morphologically informed masking regimen. abstract: arXiv:2610.31726v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Effective human-machine teaming requires agents that coordinate with unpredictable human partners. title: When and How Does Muon Precondition? The Role of Structured Gradient Noise
abstract: arXiv:2610.31728v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Muon has become a popular optimizer for large language model training, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. In this work, we study how gradient noise geometry shapes Muon's preconditioning benefits. abstract: arXiv:2610.31731v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to predict human sentiments by integrating signals from different modalities such as text, video, and audio. title: DirCast: Live Esports Directing and Commentary with a Single Streaming Video-Language Model
abstract: arXiv:2610.31734v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A live esports broadcast needs a director who chooses which camera goes on air and a caster who talks over that choice, every second and without knowing what comes next. abstract: arXiv:2610.31768v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) can jointly process a broad range of modalities, such as text, audio, and video, enabling stronger multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities, but often at substantial inference cost. title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
abstract: arXiv:2610.31778v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long horizon agentic tasks are now pushing LLM agents past their context window. To continue the task, the agent scaffold has to free up the context window, a process known as context compaction. abstract: arXiv:2610.31786v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Federated unlearning (FU) aims to remove a designated target client's influence from a trained model without the prohibitive cost of retraining from scratch. abstract: arXiv:2610.31789v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Scientific computing increasingly relies on large language model-based agents for performance engineering tasks such as instrumentation, analysis, and workflow porting. abstract: arXiv:2610.31791v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated research is largely evaluated by benchmark performance, but the value of research rarely reduces to a single score. Humans judge a work's holistic contribution through peer review, which is hard to model because it is noisy and depends on many factors. abstract: arXiv:2610.31808v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is a form of harmful language that belittles and assumes pity for vulnerable groups, reinforcing negative societal stereotypes. title: CuraLoc: Repository-Level Fault Localization via Planned Code Inspection
abstract: arXiv:2610.31809v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A bug report describes what went wrong, but rarely where the code should change. abstract: arXiv:2610.31818v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, the standard backbone for modern large-scale deep learning, employ conditional computation: only a sparse subset of model weights is used in each forward pass. abstract: arXiv:2610.31819v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speculative decoding is a technique that accelerates the inference speed of autoregressive large language models (LLMs) by sampling from a faster, lower quality draft model. abstract: arXiv:2610.31820v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reliable confidence estimation is essential for trustworthy deployment of large language models (LLMs), but dedicated confidence training stage requires additional data and compute. abstract: arXiv:2610.31821v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How well a poetry archive can be searched depends on what the user still remembers, not only on what the model understands. abstract: arXiv:2610.31835v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Temporary traffic control redirects vehicles through work zones, requiring automated vehicles to connect an interpretation of the visible devices to a continuous passing path. abstract: arXiv:2610.31840v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-calling agents are mostly optimized for accuracy; in deployment, however, their growing cost is latency: every tool call is decoded autoregressively. abstract: arXiv:2610.31842v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How do children learn the meanings of the simple, concrete words that form a majority of their early vocabulary? abstract: arXiv:2610.31846v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Intelligent agents should learn from their mistakes so that experience leads to continuous improvement. abstract: arXiv:2610.31848v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Imaging Flow Cytometry (IFC) generates large multispectral datasets, yet the need for expert annotations bottlenecks the development of supervised deep learning models.
